name: Battle of Raphia
note: The accounts give no ground for the field, so none is drawn. The Ptolemaic army is placed on the left of the plan and the Seleucid army on the right, with each king on the wing the accounts name. The accounts say the Ptolemaic right wing wheeled to avoid the panicked elephants and also that Ptolemy's cavalry on his far right routed its opponents; the plan shows both elephant contingents retreating and the far-right cavalry winning, and does not draw the wheel. The sizes of the blocks are rough and are not the numbers of men.

phases.title: The two armies drawn up
phases.text: After five days of skirmishing both kings arrayed their troops. Each put the phalanx in the centre, the light troops and mercenaries beside it, the elephants in front of them and the cavalry on the wings.
phases.quote: After five days of skirmishing, the two kings decided to array their troops for battle.

phases.title: The elephants charge and the Ptolemaic ones panic
phases.text: The elephants on both wings moved to charge. The smaller Ptolemaic African elephants retreated in panic before the larger Indian ones and ran through the infantry behind them, which fell into disorder.
phases.quote: Ptolemy's diminutive African elephants retreated in panic before the impact with the larger Indians and ran through the lines of friendly infantry arrayed behind them, causing disorder in their ranks.

phases.title: Antiochus charges the Ptolemaic horse
phases.text: Antiochus led his cavalry to the right, rode past the left wing of the Ptolemaic elephants and charged the enemy horse.
phases.quote: Antiochus had led his cavalry to the right, rode past the left wing of the Ptolemaic elephants charging the enemy horse.

phases.title: The phalanxes engage, and the Ptolemaic right wins
phases.text: The two phalanxes closed in a stiff and chaotic fight. Ptolemy rode to the centre to urge on his phalanx, which had Egyptians beside the Macedonians. On the far right the Ptolemaic cavalry routed its opponents.
phases.quote: The Ptolemaic and Seleucid phalanxes engaged in a stiff and chaotic fight.

phases.title: Antiochus routs the Ptolemaic horse and pursues
phases.text: Antiochus routed the Ptolemaic horse facing him and pursued the fleeing enemy in a mass, believing that he had won the day.
phases.quote: Antiochus routed the Ptolemaic horse posed against him and pursued the fleeing enemy en masse

phases.title: The Ptolemaic phalanx drives the Seleucids back
phases.text: The Ptolemaic phalanx drove the Seleucid phalanx back. Antiochus tried to ride back, but by then his troops were routed and could not be regrouped, and the battle was over.
phases.quote: the Ptolemaic phalanxes eventually drove the Seleucid phalanxes back and soon Antiochus realized that his judgment was wrong.
